BatchEdge.description:
One edge in a :class:`SubmitBatch`.

Each endpoint is named EITHER by batch item index (``from_index`` /
``to_index``, 0-based into ``items``) for a row created in this batch,
OR by an existing row's ``from_id`` / ``to_id`` UUID. Exactly one of
index/id must be set per endpoint. Index references are the only way to
link two brand-new rows -- inline-created targets have no id until the
batch commits. Annotations mirror :class:`CreateEdge`.
BatchEdge.title: BatchEdge

CampaignLead.description: The lead's model and effort in a canvas's campaign setup; either may be unset.
CampaignLead.title: CampaignLead

CampaignSetup.description:
A canvas's default campaign settings, any subset of them.

A launch from a chat in the canvas takes each field the asker's line leaves
unset, and the site's terms under both. Only the shape is validated here: the
terms bound and default every field at launch, where the model catalog and the
staffing grammar are known, so a value over a ceiling, or a model the site cannot
run, is refused there with a plain line, never at the write.
CampaignSetup.title: CampaignSetup

CanvasConflict.description: A stale operation's conflict response, including live state.
CanvasConflict.title: CanvasConflict

CanvasLayout.description:
A canvas's layout: resolution-free, fitted to each screen by the browser.

Every key is optional, and a write replaces only the keys it names. Widths,
sizes and places are fractions of the stage, never pixels; Chat's width is in
``ch`` (a Terminal Chat is 80 columns). The sizes are the open canvas tab's.
CanvasLayout.title: CanvasLayout

CanvasMark.description: A red box drawn on the canvas since the sender's last line, with what it covers.

CanvasMessageContext.description: Server-derived canvas context attached to an inbound message.

CanvasPage.description: A page the sender was on, with the record it shows when it names one.
CanvasPage.title: CanvasPage

CanvasPartner.description:
Who a canvas's Chat talks to now, computed on every read and never stored.

For ``assistant`` the partner is the assistant's newest live session; an assistant
with no live session is still named, as unavailable. For ``claude`` or ``codex``
it is the chat's session while a run of that CLI drains it, else ``offline``,
still naming the chat's session, so a run can be started attached to it.

CanvasRecordContext.description: A graph record the sender sees on screen, with a bounded title preview.

CanvasSettingsRefs.description: Settings rows and canvas metadata the assistant uses for a chat.
CanvasSettingsRefs.title: CanvasSettingsRefs

CanvasSummary.description: One of a user's canvases, as the canvas list shows it.

CanvasTab.description:
One of a canvas's canvas tabs.

The open tab is the canvas's canvas itself; the others keep here what they
show (the page, the visuals and their sizes) until they are opened again,
when the browser shows it through the canvas's own operations.
CanvasTab.title: CanvasTab

CanvasVisibleVisual.description: A visual present on the canvas when a message was sent.

CaptureBox.description: A red box that stood on the canvas when the picture was taken.

CaptureImage.description: The canvas as the person sees it.

CaptureTile.description: A visual on the stage, with where its body stood in the picture.

Change.description:
An append-only audit row, chained to its cause via ``caused_by``.

On the Python side the flat ``old_*`` / ``new_*`` columns collapse into
two nested :class:`Snapshot` objects. The populated fields in each name
the columns the event touched; a NULL on one side means the value came
into being or ceased to exist. The schema CHECK constraints decide which
deltas a given ``kind`` may carry.

``old`` / ``new`` is the temporal pair, kept distinct from
``edges.from_id`` / ``edges.to_id``, which are graph endpoints in a
different table.

The per-event USD spend is the difference between the sides:
:attr:`marginal_cost` returns ``new.marginal_cost - old.marginal_cost``,
treating a ``None`` side as ``Cost()``.
Change.title: Change

ChooseProvider.description:
Choose who answers the canvas's Chat; only its owner's browser does.

The switch is the next revision, and takes hold at once: from then on the chat's
queue is drained only by the new provider, and its lines go there. An assistant
turn already running is not interrupted: its answer still lands, and since every
record is read in the order of its time, it sorts where it was written. Choosing
``claude`` or ``codex`` gives the chat a session a run can attach to when it has
none, before any line, so the picker always has one to name.

Citation.description:
One inline citation on a :class:`SubmitBelief`: which artifact, how strong.

The signed ``valence`` is bounded to the same ``[-1, 1]`` the edges column
enforces, so a malformed-weight citation is rejected at the wire boundary
rather than surfacing as a mid-transaction CHECK violation. The polarity is
already resolved here (the trax ``dis*`` aliases negate before the wire), so
this is the final stored sign.
Citation.title: Citation

ClaimNextIssue.description:
Body for ``POST /api/inquiries/next_issue``: claim the next Issue.

``owner`` is who becomes responsible for the work; ``actor`` is who
performed the acquisition. They are usually the same agent, but an
orchestrator claiming on a worker's behalf needs them to differ, and the
audit must record the real performer either way.
ClaimNextIssue.title: ClaimNextIssue

ClearMarks.description: Take the boxes of one page away, or every box. No revision is expected.

The diffs hold at most ``MAX_DIFF_CHARS`` characters in all. The file that would

Posted by the browser after the per-agent sends, and carried in the context of
the message the chat's partner then receives. The partner records it in the
chat as :meth:`line` and answers nothing, but reads it in its next prompt, so it
never contradicts what the person told the agents.

Cost.description:
The two USD costs an action can incur, kept together as one value.

``agent_usd`` is the acting agent's own LLM spend; ``resource_usd`` is
any third-party compute it triggered (cloud GPUs and the like). Both
default to 0, since humans and cascade paths leave them unset. Every
``Change`` row carries its own ``Cost``, and an inquiry's total is the
sum across its log.

On disk this lives as two flat columns, ``marginal_cost_agent_usd`` and
``marginal_cost_resource_usd``, on both the inquiries table and
``change_log``. The wrapper exists so call signatures and submit models
pass one value instead of threading two floats through every layer.
Cost.title: Cost

CreateEdge.description:
Edge-create body: optional annotations.

All fields are optional; a bare ``{}`` creates an unannotated edge.
CreateEdge.title: CreateEdge

CreateEdgeBatch.description:
Batch-create body: add many edges in one round-trip.

Each item runs in its own transaction and the batch is fail-stop: on
the first item that fails, the edges already created stay committed,
the failing item reports its error, and every remaining item is
skipped (not attempted). Handy for attaching several edges at once.
CreateEdgeBatch.title: CreateEdgeBatch

CreateEdgeItem.description: One :class:`CreateEdgeBatch` item, with edge identity in the body.
CreateEdgeItem.title: CreateEdgeItem

CreateTokenBody.description:
Request body for minting an API key.

``name`` is a human-facing label stored on the key so the UI can show
what runs from where. ``role`` is an optional per-key ceiling that
defaults to the caller's own role; a stronger role is rejected with
403, which lets a writer mint a viewer-only token for a read-only
agent without losing their own write capability.

``open_into`` pins the one audience the key opens sessions into. It may not exceed
what the caller opens into: an audience beyond that is 403, and a name that is no
audience is 422. A key minted by another key that leaves it out inherits that
key's pin.
CreateTokenBody.title: CreateTokenBody

EvidenceTimelineResponse.description: The bounded response contract consumed by the generated web client.
EvidenceTimelineResponse.title: EvidenceTimelineResponse

ExecRequest.description: One command to run on a machine.
ExecRequest.title: ExecRequest

FeedActorFacet.description: One session's share of a feed window, as the console's agent list shows it.
FeedActorFacet.title: FeedActorFacet

FeedCursor.description:
A keyset cursor into the feed's ``(created, session_id, part, seq)`` order.

The cursor must carry EVERY order-key component, not just ``created``: a
page boundary can fall inside a group of rows sharing a ``created``
instant, and a bare-``created`` resume (``> created``) would skip every
tied row after it. ``part`` joined the key when the feed moved to IR
records, since ``seq`` restarts within each source file.
FeedCursor.title: FeedCursor

FeedEvent.description:
One captured turn plus the session context the console needs.

The cross-session feed (the multi-agent console) interleaves turns from
every session into one time-ordered stream, so each item must carry which
session it came from and that session's routing identity -- unlike a
record read through :mod:`wire.wire_session_ir`, which is always read in
the context of one known session and part. ``created`` (the server write
clock) is the feed's order key, not the per-part ``seq``, because ``seq``
is only monotonic within a part.
FeedEvent.title: FeedEvent

FeedFacetsResponse.description:
What a feed window holds, by session, room and record kind.

``actors`` is newest ``last`` first; ``rooms`` and ``kinds`` are largest
``count`` first.
FeedFacetsResponse.title: FeedFacetsResponse

FeedHistogramResponse.description:
Feed records per time bucket, every bucket from ``start`` to ``end``.

Buckets are ``bucket_seconds`` wide and aligned to the Unix epoch, so the
first starts at or before the window's start and the last ends after its
end; buckets with no records are listed with a ``count`` of 0.
FeedHistogramResponse.title: FeedHistogramResponse

FeedKindFacet.description: One record kind's share of a feed window.
FeedKindFacet.title: FeedKindFacet

FeedResponse.description:
One page of the cross-session console feed, oldest first.

``events`` is ordered by ``(created, session_id, part, seq)`` so the console can
append in order and resume from ``next_after`` on its next poll. The cursor
is composite (see :class:`FeedCursor`) so a same-``created`` tie split
across a page boundary is not skipped. ``next_after`` is ``None`` only when
the page is empty and no prior cursor was supplied (a poll that drained the
tail echoes back the cursor it was given).
FeedResponse.title: FeedResponse

FeedRoomFacet.description: One room's share of a feed window.
FeedRoomFacet.title: FeedRoomFacet

FieldDraft.description: The unsent text of one field's editor, and the value editing began from.
FieldDraft.title: FieldDraft

FieldMutation.description:
Base body for every per-field mutation: ``actor`` plus ``reason``.

This is the whole body for DELETE (unset). PUT and PATCH extend it
with ``value`` (and PUT adds ``expected`` for compare-and-set).
FieldMutation.title: FieldMutation

HeartbeatResponse.description: The server's clock at the heartbeat, and whether the host must be upgraded.

Highlight.description: Mark inquiries on the browser's page. An event, as navigate is.

InboundDrainItem.description:
One message drained for a session, with its attested sender.

The drain **response** item: unlike the enqueue request, it carries
``source`` -- the producer's attested ``--as`` / principal -- so the
poller can render the ``[room] sender:`` injection context. Inbound-only
and transient: it is **not** an ``agent_session_events`` row; when the
agent consumes it, the capture path logs it as a normal turn.
InboundDrainItem.title: InboundDrainItem

InboundEnqueueRequest.description:
A message a client asks trackinizer to inject into a live session.

The enqueue **request** carries ``text`` -- the one field the route delivers --
and, from the configured assistant alone, the ``asker`` it sends for. ``source``
is attested by the route from the authenticated principal (a client cannot forge
another sender), and ``room`` has no enqueue semantics (the direct-session
enqueue route discards it; routed delivery is the separate ``@actor:room``
send-message path). ``extra="forbid"`` makes a client-sent ``source`` or ``room``
a 422 rather than a silently-ignored field -- the request and response shapes are
deliberately distinct (the response :class:`InboundDrainItem` carries both
``source`` and ``room``), so neither can be confused for the other.
InboundEnqueueRequest.title: InboundEnqueueRequest

InboundEnqueueResponse.description:
Receipt for an enqueued inbound message.

``queued`` is the current count pending for the session after this enqueue,
including on an idempotent retry. It is
an honest receipt -- the message is queued for the session's poller, not
proven delivered; a session whose run is gone never drains it.
InboundEnqueueResponse.title: InboundEnqueueResponse

What one part's source file is, re-sent with every append batch.

Re-sent rather than written once because it CHANGES as the file grows:
``records`` counts what has arrived, and the encoding a reader reports is
only correct for the prefix it has consumed -- claude's ascii-escaping
convention is a majority that is not decided until the stream ends.
ManifestBody.title: ManifestBody

Mark.title: Mark

MarkCovers.description: What lies under a mark, read from the page when it was drawn.
MarkCovers.title: MarkCovers

MarkPoint.description: A place on the stage, as fractions of its width and height.
MarkPoint.title: MarkPoint

MetricMaskClause.description:
One ``at <axis> <op> <value>`` mask clause.

``op`` is either a :data:`MetricCompareOp` comparison (``is`` / ``ne`` /
``lt`` / ``le`` / ``gt`` / ``ge``), carrying a ``value``, or a step-axis
reduction (``max`` / ``min``) with ``value`` empty. The server combines
every clause with AND into one SQL predicate over ``experiment_metrics``,
and refuses a comparison ``value`` that no stored cell could hold on its
axis (see :class:`~wire.wire_metrics.MetricPoint`).
MetricMaskClause.title: MetricMaskClause

MetricPoint.description:
One logged metric point, as sent over the wire.

The wire carrier for an
:class:`~types.experiment_metrics.ExperimentMetric`. ``(key, step)`` is
the dedup key together with the owning ``experiment_id`` (supplied in the
path, not the body): a repeated point is a no-op. ``value`` is the scalar;
``kind`` discriminates the shape (``"scalar"`` today).
MetricPoint.title: MetricPoint

MetricQueryRequest.description:
A mask over the metric grid plus one operation on the masked selection.

``masks`` AND together. ``write`` set means assign that value to every
masked cell (a bulk upsert); ``write`` unset makes it a read, ordered by
``sort`` (over the value, ties by cell) and windowed by ``limit`` (unset
reads up to ``MAX_LIST_LIMIT`` cells). ``sort`` / ``limit`` apply to reads
only and are rejected alongside a ``write``; the read and rank routes
likewise reject a ``write``.
MetricQueryRequest.title: MetricQueryRequest

MetricQueryResponse.description: The masked cells of a read, in ``(key, step)`` order.
MetricQueryResponse.title: MetricQueryResponse

MetricRankRequest.description:
A cross-experiment metric query: the same mask, over many experiments.

The experiments are named one of two ways: ``experiment_ids`` the caller
preselected, or ``filters`` -- the inquiry list's ``{field, op, value}``
clauses, ANDed over the Experiment rows -- which the server runs in the
same query, so a selection of any size needs no id list. The ``mask``
then reads/ranks their grids together. This is the leaderboard surface --
there is no stored ranking, only this query plus the ``sort`` / ``limit``
/ ``offset`` on the inner :class:`MetricQueryRequest`.
MetricRankRequest.title: MetricRankRequest

MetricRankResponse.description: The cross-experiment masked cells, ordered by the query's sort.
MetricRankResponse.title: MetricRankResponse

MetricRankRow.description: One cell of a cross-experiment read, tagged with its experiment.
MetricRankRow.title: MetricRankRow

MetricWriteResponse.description:
How many cells a masked ``to`` write upserted.

``written`` counts cells newly inserted or updated by the assignment; a
bulk write over a wide mask reports the full count so the caller sees the
blast radius.
MetricWriteResponse.title: MetricWriteResponse

SubmitBatch.description:
Batch-submit body: collapse N submit round-trips into one.

Each item routes by its ``kind`` discriminator just like an
individual submit route. The batch is ALL-OR-NOTHING: every item and
every edge is created in one shared transaction, so a single failure
rolls the whole batch back and no row or edge is persisted. Per-item
idempotency keys are required so a retried batch re-probes and returns
the originally created ids instead of duplicating rows.

``edges`` wire newly-created rows together by item index, so one
request can create a row plus an inline-created neighbour and link
them atomically -- the case a flat list of rows cannot express.

get.description: Describe every addon of this deployment without touching its services.

List allowlist entries for the admin page.

Args:
  request: FastAPI Request object containing app state with db engine.
  identity: Admin identity from authentication dependency.

Returns:

    added_by, added_at.

post.description:
Insert a new allowlist entry; 409 on a duplicate ``email_or_pattern``.

The 409 comes from the global unique-violation handler in
``api.app``, so this route needs no try/except of its own. An entry at the
service-account domain, an address or ``*@service.invalid``, answers 422: a
service account never signs in.

Args:
  body: Request body with email_or_pattern and role to add.
  request: FastAPI Request object containing app state with db engine.
  identity: Admin identity from authentication dependency.

Returns:
  confirmation: Success flag, canonical email_or_pattern, and role.

delete.description:
Delete one allowlist entry by its (URL-decoded) primary key.

Clients URL-encode ``*@example.com`` as ``%2A%40example.com``;
Starlette percent-decodes path params before the handler sees them,
so the value matches the stored row as-is.

Args:
  email_or_pattern: Email address or domain wildcard pattern to delete.
  request: FastAPI Request object containing app state with db engine.
  identity: Admin identity from authentication dependency.

Returns:
  confirmation: Success flag only.

put.description:
Change one allowlist entry's role; 404 when the key matches no row.

Same URL-decode behavior as the DELETE route: clients percent-encode
wildcard rows like ``*@example.com`` as ``%2A%40example.com`` and
FastAPI hands the path param back already decoded.

Args:
  email_or_pattern: Email address or domain wildcard pattern to match.
  body: Request body with new role assignment.
  request: FastAPI Request object containing app state with db engine.
  identity: Admin identity from authentication dependency.

Returns:
  confirmation: Success flag and updated role.

Lock or unlock one inquiry; admin only.

Args:
  target_id: The inquiry to lock or unlock.
  body: Whether it is locked from now on.
  request: The request, which carries the store.
  identity: Authenticated admin.

Returns:
  result: The inquiry's ``id`` and its ``locked`` flag.

post.description:
Create a service account; 409 when its name is taken, whatever the row's status.

A disabled account keeps its name until an admin deletes it, so creating the name
again never revives it; a deleted account takes its keys with it, and a new account
of the same name starts with none. The account holds the audiences the staff
setting gives its address, and a caller cannot create one that holds more than it
does.

Args:
  body: The account's name and role.
  request: Request carrying the database engine and the configuration.
  identity: Admin principal, recorded in the log as who created it.

Returns:
  user: The new user, as ``GET /api/admin/users`` lists one.

Raises:
  HTTPException: 403 when the account would hold an audience the caller does not,
    409 when the name is taken.

get.description:
List the keys of a service account, never a secret or a hash.

Args:
  user_id: The service account.
  request: Request carrying the database engine.
  identity: Admin principal.

Returns:
  tokens: Every key of the account, live and revoked, newest first.

Raises:
  HTTPException: 404 when the id is no service account, a person's included.

post.description:
Mint one API key for a service account; the secret is shown once.

The key's role is at most the account's and defaults to it. Its pin stays
inside the audiences the account holds under the staff setting, and inside what
the caller's own credential reads and opens into; a pinned key hands its pin on.
The account row stays locked until the key is stored, so a disable cannot slip
between the check and the insert.

Args:
  user_id: The service account.
  body: The key's label, and optionally its role and pin.
  request: Request carrying the database engine and the configuration.
  response: Response, marked ``no-store`` because it carries a secret.
  identity: Admin principal, recorded in the log as who minted it.

Returns:
  token: The key's id, label, prefix, role, stored pin and plaintext secret.

Raises:
  HTTPException: 403 when the role or the pin exceeds the account's or the
    caller's, 404 when the id is no service account, 409 when it is disabled.

Revoke one key of a service account.

Unknown id, another account's key, and an already revoked key all answer 404, as
does an id that is no service account: the route never reaches a person's keys.

Args:
  user_id: The service account.
  key_id: The key to revoke.
  request: Request carrying the database engine and the bearer cache.
  identity: Admin principal, recorded in the log as who revoked it.

Returns:
  result: ``{"ok": true}``.

Raises:
  HTTPException: 404 when the account or its live key is not found.

get.description:
List every user row for the admin table.

Args:
  request: FastAPI Request object containing app state with db engine.
  identity: Admin identity from authentication dependency.

Returns:
  users: List of user records with id, email, name, role, status, created_at,
    last_login, and ``staff``, read-only: whether the deployment's staff setting
    makes the user staff. No route writes it.

delete.description:
Hard-delete a user, cascading their API keys and nulling audit links.

The ``api_keys.user_id`` FK cascades, so the user's keys vanish in
the same statement. The ``change_log.api_key_id`` FK sets null on
delete, so audit rows survive: only the per-key linkage is lost,
while ``actor`` and every other column stay intact.

Self-delete is refused with 409 so an admin can't accidentally lock
the org out. A multi-admin org still rotates admins by having one
admin delete the other.

Args:
  user_id: UUID of the user to delete.
  request: FastAPI Request object containing app state with db engine.
  identity: Admin identity from authentication dependency.

Returns:
  empty: 204 response with no content.

post.description:
Disable a user and revoke every API key they own.

The status change and the revocation share one transaction, so a
failed revoke can't leave a disabled user holding live tokens.

Args:
  user_id: UUID of the user to disable.
  request: FastAPI Request object containing app state with db engine.
  identity: Admin identity from authentication dependency.

Returns:
  confirmation: Success flag and new status 'disabled'.

Re-enable a previously disabled user.

Revoked tokens stay revoked; the user mints fresh keys via ``/me``,
matching the rotate-on-suspicion stance across the auth surface.

Args:
  user_id: UUID of the user to enable.
  request: FastAPI Request object containing app state with db engine.
  identity: Admin identity from authentication dependency.

Returns:
  confirmation: Success flag and new status 'active'.

delete.description:
Put a user's preferences back to their defaults, without reading them.

A person's preferences are theirs: an admin may reset them, never read them.
So this answers nothing, and no admin route returns them (``USER_COLUMNS``
leaves the column out). It writes no change row, as no preference write does.

Args:
  user_id: UUID of the user whose preferences are reset.
  request: FastAPI Request object containing app state with db engine.
  identity: Admin identity from authentication dependency.

Returns:
  empty: 204 response with no content.

put.description:
Update one user's role; 404 when the id matches no row.

A service account is a viewer or a writer: promoting one to admin answers 422.

Args:

  body: Request body with new role assignment.
  request: FastAPI Request object containing app state with db engine.
  identity: Admin identity from authentication dependency.

Returns:
  confirmation: Success flag and updated role.

post.description:
Post a line to a science chat, or start one, and queue it for the assistant.

A chat's starter, each person it is shared with and, when the server's
``TRACKINIZER_CHAT_ORGS`` is ``domain``, the starter's organisation post into it,
holding its audience; a viewer may not. Anyone else, everyone else a ``single``
server lets read it included, is refused with 403 ``chat_not_shared`` and nothing
is queued, whatever the post's ``kind``, and whether the chat is named by
``conversation_id`` or by the ``Idempotency-Key`` of a post that names none: a
line goes to the starter's own run, under its sender's name. A reader forks a
chat from one of its lines (``fork``
names it); a fork from a line of a chat the poster does not read is 422, since it
would copy lines they may not read, a fork of a ``private`` or ``staff`` chat is
409 ``chat_fork_closed``, since its copies would not keep the audience, a fork
that the poster's organisation would read and the chat's readers do not
include is 409 ``chat_fork_wider``, and a fork whose key names a conversation
someone else began is refused with 409. A
line under the id of a
deleted chat, named or as a fork's key, or a fork from a line of one, is refused
with 410 ``chat_deleted``: no chat starts under that id again. A canvas holds one
chat: its first line binds the canvas to the line's conversation, and a line
naming another conversation is refused with 409, as is one for a conversation
another canvas of the poster holds. A fork goes to a new canvas, copied from
the one it was sent from and named in the answer's ``canvas_id``. The line's
poster is the attested identity, never anything in the body. The answer is the
conversation id at once: the conversation's session appears when the assistant
opens it, and ``GET /api/chats/{id}`` finds it. A retry under the same key
queues nothing again.

The poster's canvas's provider answers, or in a chat someone else started, the
provider of its starter's canvas. ``assistant`` takes a ``line``, an ``answer`` or
an ``interrupt`` (422 for any other ``kind``); an ``answer`` is a choice on a card
the assistant asked, and an ``interrupt`` stops the turn it is on, each queued for
the chat's own session and 409 ``provider_offline`` while the assistant does not
have the chat open. For ``claude`` or ``codex`` the post, with
its ``kind`` and ``payload``, joins the queue of the chat's session that the CLI's
run drains; with no such run live it is 409 ``provider_offline``, and while the run
reports ``taken_over``, its CLI opened in a terminal, it is 409 ``chat_taken_over``
with nothing queued: reattach first. A fork from a ``claude`` or
``codex`` canvas is one too: its new session is opened at once and its line
waits there for the run the person starts.

A ``line`` that starts with a known slash command of claude or codex is judged
by the chat's provider, not the poster's canvas. One the provider runs from
Chat (``/goal``, and claude's ``/compact``) is queued as a ``command``, typed
bare, with no page, trail or marks; ``/model <name>`` and ``/effort <level>``
are queued as a ``settings`` post the same way (bare, they are refused); any
other is 422 ``command_refused`` with the reason in ``message``, and nothing is queued. Every other ``/`` line stays a
line. An ``answer`` for ``claude`` or ``codex`` is the chat's starter's alone, the
run's owner, since it runs a tool or grants trust on their machine. An ``answer``
to the assistant's card is the person's the card asked (``input.asker``, else the
starter's), since it lists their own choices, and it carries a line's page, trail
and marks. Anyone else is 403 ``answer_not_owner``, and nothing is queued. It names
the option taken (``{prompt_id, option}``), or in the older form a ``decision``.

A ``line`` may name ``attachments``, the box paths of files the poster uploaded
for it (``POST /api/chats/uploads``); they reach the assistant in the line's
context. A chat whose provider is not the assistant is 409
``uploads_unsupported`` for a line that names any, and nothing is queued.

Args:

  identity: The signed-in writer, who must own the canvas.
  key: Required retry-safe idempotency key.

Returns:

    was queued on it.

List inquiries across one or more ``kind`` query params.

Results from every requested kind are concatenated, one block per
DISTINCT kind: a repeated ``kind`` param yields one block, not several.
``limit`` and
``offset`` apply per kind, since each kind runs its own query. At
least one ``kind`` is required. Each ``seq_range`` param is one
inclusive ``a..b`` interval; their union selects rows across disjoint
seq windows in a single query.

Each ``fields`` param names one key every row keeps; the others are left
out. A key only another kind's rows carry is absent from this kind's. The
edges are read only when a relation (``narrows``, ``proved_by``, ...) is
named. Without ``fields`` each row is whole.

``ancestors=narrows`` adds ``ancestors`` to each row, after ``fields``: the
Issues it narrows, theirs, and so on up to the roots, nearest first, each
as ``{id, kind, seq, title, status, child_ids}``. ``child_ids`` names which
of the row and its listed ancestors narrow that one, so a row with several
parents keeps them all. The walk stops 8 levels up and at 200 ancestors
for the whole response, nearest first.

transcript the caller reads (its audience, and for a science chat its members); a
session the caller does not read is neither found by it nor ruled out by it.

Args:

  identity: Authenticated user identity, viewer-role-gated.

post.description:
Submit many inquiries in one all-or-nothing transaction.

Every item commits together or none does: a single failure rolls the
whole batch back, so no partial state is left behind. On success the
response is ``{"ids": [...]}`` with the server-minted ids in input
order. A failure propagates as the same HTTP error a single submit of
that item would raise (e.g. 409 on a conflict, 422 on bad input). One
item carrying ``modified`` from a non-admin 403s the batch.

Args:
  req: SubmitBatch payload with items and edges to create atomically.
  request: FastAPI request object; used to fetch the store.
  identity: Authenticated writer; enforced by Depends(require_role("writer")).

Returns:
  body: JSON object with "ids" key mapping to list of minted server IDs.

Resolve many ``UUID -> kind`` mappings in one round-trip.

``max_length`` is a typed cap on the decoded list's LENGTH: FastAPI
parses the whole body first, then rejects an oversize list with 422. It
bounds how many ids a handler will look up, NOT how many bytes the server
will read -- a 4GB body measured 30.77s of buffering before its 422.
There is NO byte bound in this application: counting bytes in an ASGI
``receive`` does not stop a chunked sender (measured against both a
hand-rolled middleware and Starlette's own ``max_body_size``: 50MB
consumed against a 1MB limit). A real bound belongs to whatever owns the
socket -- uvicorn or the reverse proxy. (REV-OPUS-30 recorded this cap;
its "pre-decode" claim was wrong.) The response
is ``{"found": {id: kind}, "missing": [id]}`` so a caller learns which
ids were unknown rather than having them silently dropped from a flat
mapping (REV-OPUS-12).

Args:
  ids: List of UUIDs to resolve; capped at MAX_LIST_LIMIT by FastAPI.
  request: FastAPI request object for middleware access.
  identity: Authenticated user identity, viewer-role-gated.

Returns:
  body: Mapping with "found" (id->kind dict) and "missing" (unknown ids).

Register the machine if it is new and issue a one-use enrollment token.

A new token supersedes any open one for the same machine. An admin enrolls a
machine that is new, unowned or already theirs, and confirms it; one another person
owns answers 409 ``machine_owned``, naming the owner. A writer may enroll a machine
that is new, which becomes theirs with the role ``personal`` and stays unconfirmed
until they confirm it in the web app, or one that is already theirs.

The configured assistant may name an ``asker``, a writer or admin it answers. The
machine is then the asker's: personal, confirmed, and theirs to open a terminal on,
and the token joins only for them. The assistant owns nothing it enrolls.

Args:

  request: Request carrying the database engine.
  response: Response, marked ``no-store`` because it carries a secret.
  identity: Writer principal, recorded as who enrolled the machine.

Returns:

Raises:
  ValidationError: The name is reserved.
  MachineOwnedError: An admin names a machine another person owns.
  HTTPException: 403 when a writer names a machine that is not theirs, or anyone
    but the assistant names an asker, or the asker is no active writer.

The token is the credential, so the route has no other authentication. It is
valid once, within 15 minutes, for the machine name it was issued for, and only
while the account that issued it is still an active admin, or owns the machine and
it is a personal one.
Joining a machine that already has a live credential revokes that credential first
and closes the terminals open on it.

  request: Request carrying the database engine.

Raises:

One host instance holds a machine at a time. Under ``keep`` a different instance

holds the machine leaves it held by none, so it reads offline; from any other
instance it changes nothing.

Args:

  request: Request carrying the database engine.

Returns:

The host learns of it by a 410 on its next request, and its terminals and

Run a command on the asker's machine and return what it produced.

Only the configured assistant calls this, naming an attested writer or admin

reports, up to the command's ``timeout_sec`` and a short grace. A retry under the
same ``Idempotency-Key`` is told what the first try was, its result or its 504 or
410 once the host was handed the command, and runs nothing twice. A command that
was refused, or that no host took, is run by the retry. The machine must be online,
confirmed by its owner, and report ``exec: true``.

Args:

    ``exec_limit`` past 60 commands a minute for the asker; 504 ``exec_lost`` when

post.description:
Resolve a routing name to live sessions and enqueue the message.

The ergonomic front door for ``trax send``: the server resolves ``actor``
(optionally scoped to ``room``) to the live sessions that match and
enqueues the text to each, so the caller never needs a session id. Sender
is route-attested (the principal), never the body. Delivery is
drop-if-absent -- the response lists the sessions enqueued; an empty list
means no live session matched.

Policy: any ``writer`` may message the agent of any session whose audience it
reads. The configured assistant may message one it does not read only for an
``asker`` it names, who is that session's account or a writer who holds its
audience: it relays a user's line and passes on that user's rights, not its own.
Sessions are a shared canvas and cross-agent messaging is the feature, so there
is no per-opener ownership gate here (or on the direct ``/inbound`` route). The
sender is always truthfully attested. When any live session the name resolves to
is one the sender may not message, the whole send is 403 ``session_audience`` and
nothing is queued, so a send never reports a delivery that did not happen.

A science chat is reached through its canvas, so a browser's send to one is
refused with 409 ("Open its canvas to talk to this chat"), whether or not the
chat is being drained; an agent key's send to a chat being drained is refused
with 409 too.

A bare ``actor`` (no ``room``) is rejected when the matched session belongs
to more than one room: a single PTY interleaves every room's messages, so
the caller must name the room (``@actor:room``) to give the agent context.
Retries that reuse the request's ``Idempotency-Key`` return the original
receipt without re-enqueuing (the send path writes no ``change_log`` row to
dedup against), but only a delivery that reached at least one live session
is recorded: an empty send leaves the key unrecorded so a later retry --
once the session is live -- still delivers instead of replaying nothing.

Args:
  body: Message text and optional room scope to address by actor name, and the
    user the assistant sends it for.
  request: Starlette request object.
  identity: Authenticated user (sender is attested, not from body).

Returns:
  response: SendMessageResponse with list of (session_id,
    message_count) pairs of all sessions enqueued (may be empty if no
    live session matched).

Open a session: mint an ``AgentSession`` row and return its server id.

The session ``owner`` doubles as the routing name (``--as``). It is made
unique among live sessions (suffix on collision); the granted name is the
owner stamped on the row and is echoed in the response so the run
adopts whatever it was given.

The session opens into the audience the caller's key is pinned to, else
``open``, or ``private`` when ``private`` asks; a pin the caller no longer holds
is 403 ``audience_not_held``, and so is ``private`` under a pin to ``staff``. A
resume asked to be ``private`` hides the ``open`` session it re-attaches, as the
key that opened it may, and is 409, leaving it as it was, for a ``staff`` one. A
session under the id of a science chat that is not ``open`` takes the chat's
audience instead, so a chat stays ``private`` or ``staff`` whichever key opens
its next session; a chat's first session takes ``private`` when the canvas that
holds the chat chose it (its ``opens_as``). A ``cli_session_id`` of a deleted
science chat (``chat:<id>``) is 410 ``chat_deleted``. A science chat's session is
titled ``Science chat`` whatever ``title`` says, since every key reads the row and
only the chat's members read its lines.

``attach`` re-opens that session by its id instead: it is live again if it had
ended, its ``cli_session_id`` stays, and the run's file becomes its next part. The
response names it as a fresh start's would. A caller who may not write the
session is 403, and so is one a science chat takes no run from: only its opening
key, the assistant's or its starter's attach to a chat. An unknown id is 404.

Args:
  body: Session metadata (title, cli, cli_session_id, attach, started, rooms,
    account, idempotency_key, private).
  request: Starlette request object.
  identity: Authenticated user (email, api_key_id, role).

Returns:
  response: SessionStartResponse with session id, next event seq (0 for
    new, or max(seq)+1 for resumed), cli_session_id, granted actor name and
    audience.

Make a session ``private``, or ``open`` again; for a chat, every one under its id.

Only its owner does, from a browser or by key: anyone else, an admin included,
is 403 ``session_not_owner``. A ``staff`` session is 409 ``session_staff``. Each
session that moves is audited in the change log; asking for the audience it has
moves nothing.

Args:
  session_id: The session.
  body: The audience it takes.
  request: Request carrying the store.
  identity: The caller.

Returns:
  response: The session, its audience, and every session that moved.

Close a session atomically and release its inbound queue.

``end_session`` stamps ``ended`` + ``status`` (and backfills
``cli_session_id`` when given) in one transaction, so a partial
failure can never leave a zombie session -- ``ended`` set yet
``status`` non-terminal -- and the inbound queue is drained only after
the close commits, so a failed end never silently discards undelivered
steering messages. A second end on an already-closed session is a 409. A
session whose audience the caller neither reads nor opened is 403
``session_audience``. A science chat is closed by a key that may run on it: its
opening key, the assistant's or its starter's (403 otherwise); its starter may also
close it from a browser, which has no key. An end that names
a ``cli`` other than the chat's provider is a 200 that changes nothing: it is the
exit of a run a switch stopped, and the session is the chat's, now drained by the
provider its canvas chose. An end that names a ``cli`` and an ``instance`` is
the same 200 that changes nothing when the run it names was replaced, or another
run of that CLI holds the session's lease: it is the exit of a run a reattach
took over, and the run holding the chat goes on. Any other end first releases
the asks the run left open: an ``$interaction_resolved`` record with
``by: released`` for each, which the
closed session would take no more.

Args:
  session_id: UUID of the session to close.
  body: Session status, optional cli_session_id backfill, and the ending run's
    CLI and instance.
  request: Starlette request object.
  identity: Authenticated user (audit actor for the change).

Returns:
  response: SessionEndResponse with session id and committed ended
    timestamp (original value on idempotent replay).

get.description:
Drain all pending inbound messages for a session (oldest first).

Read by the session's run to inject queued messages into the CLI.
A viewer key may drain only the session it opened. Unknown session -> 404.

``wait_sec`` holds the request open until a message arrives, so the caller
waits instead of asking repeatedly: one held request per session rather
than one round trip per interval, and delivery on arrival rather than up
to an interval late. Zero (the default) returns whatever is pending now,
preserving the original contract for any caller that does not want to
block. The ceiling keeps a held request shorter than the idle timeout of
a proxy that would otherwise cut it. Ending the session ends the hold, so
the run that ends it as it exits is not kept waiting on its own poller.

The drain is 403 ``session_audience`` unless the caller opened the session or reads
its audience.

Writers retain shared access to the drains of ordinary sessions, but a science
chat and the assistant's service session are drained by their opening key alone
(403 otherwise). Viewer access is scoped to the opening API key so reading chat
does not grant graph-write permission.

A science chat's queue has one drainer, the provider its starter's canvas names,
and one live run. For ``claude`` or ``codex`` a drain by the configured assistant's
key is 409 ``provider_is_cli``, and the run that drains it may be under any key a
chat takes a run from (its opening key or its starter's; 403 otherwise). For
``assistant`` a drain by its opening key that is not the assistant's is 409
``provider_is_assistant``. Either holds from the moment the canvas switches.

A chat answered by a CLI is drained by a run that names its ``cli``: a drain that
names none, as a ``trax`` older than the name sends, is 426 ``cli_required`` and
takes no lease, since the server cannot tell which CLI polls. A drain by the other
CLI than the canvas's is 409 ``provider_is_other_cli``. The lease records the
named CLI, and the chat is live for a provider only while a poller that named it
holds the lease. ``instance`` is an id the run minted for itself; a drain whose
``instance`` differs from that of the unexpired lease of the same CLI is 409
``chat_run_live``, so one chat never has two runs draining it. So is a drain by
a run the server replaced when it reattached the chat (``POST .../reattach``).

A drain of a CLI chat's session that has ended, as when the person closed the chat,
is 409 ``session_ended`` and the run stops; a session the reaper closed for silence
is reopened by the drain instead.

``run``, ``machine`` and ``cwd`` say where the draining run is, and the lease the
drain takes keeps them for Chat to show (a malformed one is 422). They are the
caller's own word about its own run, shown and never trusted; a run that names
none is shown as it was before runs named themselves.

Args:
  session_id: UUID of the session to drain messages from.
  request: Starlette request object.
  identity: Authenticated reader and, for viewers, the opening key.
  wait_sec: Seconds to hold the request open for a message to arrive
    (clamped to [0, 30]; 0 returns queued messages immediately).
  run: The name of the detached run, which an attach takes; absent for a run in
    a terminal of its own.
  machine: The run's machine, as the machine host names it.
  cwd: The run's working directory, ``~/...`` under its home: at most 1,024
    characters, none of them a control character.
  cli: The CLI the draining run is, as the run names it: a lowercase word of
    at most 32 characters.
  instance: The run's own id, 32 lowercase hexadecimal digits, the same on each of
    its drains.

Returns:
  response: DrainInboundResponse with list of pending messages (text, kind,
    payload, source, room), oldest first, or empty list if none are queued.

post.description:
Enqueue a message to inject into a live session's input.

The sender is **attested by the route**, never trusted from the body: the
stored ``source`` is always the authenticated principal, so an agent
cannot forge another sender. The request body (:class:`InboundEnqueueRequest`)
carries no ``source`` at all -- a client that sends one gets 422, not a
silently-ignored field. The session must exist and have a recent inbound
poll; an ended or stale session is rejected (409) because no poller will
drain it. A session whose audience the sender does not read is 403
``session_audience``, unless the sender is the configured assistant sending for
an ``asker`` who is that session's account or a writer who holds its audience.

Args:
  session_id: UUID of the session to message.
  body: Message text to inject, and the user the assistant sends it for.
  request: Starlette request object.
  identity: Authenticated user (sender is attested, not from body).

Returns:
  response: InboundEnqueueResponse with list of (session_id,
    message_count) pairs of sessions enqueued (always the one target).

get.description:
Read the answer the chat's assistant is writing, once it is not the one seen.

Answers at once when the held partial's ``seq`` is not ``after``; else when it
changes, or when it expires; else after ``wait_sec`` with it unchanged. 404
``chat_partials_off`` when the server streams no answers, 404 for no session,
and 403 ``session_audience`` to a caller who does not read the session's records,
asked again before a changed partial is answered.

Args:
  session_id: The chat's session.
  request: Request carrying the store and the partials.
  identity: A reader of the chat.
  after: The ``seq`` the caller last saw; 0 for none.
  wait_sec: Seconds to hold the request for a change, clamped to [0, 25].

Returns:
  state: The partial held, and its ``seq``; ``seq`` 0 and none when none is.

put.description:
Hold the answer a chat's assistant is writing, in place of the one held.

Refused in this order: 404 ``chat_partials_off`` when the server streams no
answers; 403 ``not_the_assistant`` from anyone but the configured assistant; 404
for no session; 404 ``not_a_chat`` for a session that is no science chat; 403
from a key that did not open the session; 409 ``session_ended`` once it ended.

Args:
  session_id: The chat's session.
  body: The answer so far, its turn, and whether it is whole.
  request: Request carrying the store and the partials.
  identity: The assistant, by the key that opened the session.

Returns:
  response: Empty.

delete.description:
Drop the chat's partial if it is of ``turn``; a later turn's stays.

Refused as a put is, but for an ended session, whose partial may still go.

Args:
  session_id: The chat's session.
  turn: The turn whose partial ends.
  request: Request carrying the store and the partials.
  identity: The assistant, by the key that opened the session.

Returns:
  response: Empty, whether or not a partial was dropped.

get.description:
List the files this session was captured from, in ``part`` order.

Args:
  session_id: AgentSession ID to list parts from.
  request: FastAPI request (carries auth and store).
  identity: Authenticated reader.
  asker: The account the configured assistant reads for.
  chat: The conversation the configured assistant reads into.

Returns:
  result: ReadPartsResponse with manifest info for each part.

post.description:
Place a session in the caller's workspace and a canvas; the server decides.

The first rule that matches wins: the canvas the run started from, when it is the
caller's; the placement the session already has; the workspace of the caller's
newest earlier session on the same git branch, in a new canvas; else the caller's
default workspace, in a new canvas. Placing a placed session returns its
placement. A service account's session and a science chat are not placed: both
ids are null.

Args:
  session_id: The session, which the caller's own key opened.
  body: The canvas the run started from, and its git checkout.
  request: Request carrying the database engine and store.
  identity: The session's own account and key.

Returns:
  placement: The workspace and canvas of the session.

Reopen a chat's run headless, where it ran, after a terminal took it over.

The chat's run keeps its CLI session: the new run attaches to the chat's session,
which resumes the CLI's own stored session, on the machine and in the folder the
last run named. When a person opened the CLI in a terminal, that run is replaced:
its lease is revoked and it is turned away when it drains again, which ends its
terminal, and the terminals this server opened for it are stopped. The run starts
as a detached host of the old run's name (``chat-<session>`` for a run that named
none): a launch of that name ends the old host and resumes the CLI session its
terminal continued.

Only the chat's starter reattaches it, from their own browser. A chat whose run is
live and not taken over is 409 ``chat_run_live``, and one whose machine or folder
the server does not know (it restarted since the run last polled) is 409
``reattach_place_unknown``. The machine and CLI are held to the rules of an open:
404 for a machine that is not online, 409 ``cli_not_installed``,
``terminal_unconfirmed`` and ``terminal_not_enabled``. A retry under the same
``Idempotency-Key`` opens one run.

Args:
  session_id: The chat's session, as the Chat or the Console row names it.
  request: Request carrying the store, the terminal hub and the inbound queue.
  identity: The signed-in starter.
  key: Required retry-safe idempotency key.

Raises:
  HTTPException: 403 ``terminal_forbidden`` for a key, a service account or a
    foreign origin, 403 ``reattach_not_owner`` for anyone but the chat's starter;
    404 for no such session; 409 ``not_a_chat``, ``provider_is_assistant``,
    ``chat_run_live``, ``reattach_place_unknown``; 429 ``terminal_limit`` past 10
    opens a minute.

get.description:
Read one page of a part's records.

``after_idx`` is an EXCLUSIVE lower bound rather than an offset, so paging
is stable while a capture is still appending: an offset would re-window
every time the part grew.

``plaintext_only`` skips the ciphertext splice, which is what a viewer
wants -- only a replay needs the encrypted half, and it is the largest
thing on the row.

Args:
  session_id: AgentSession ID to read from.
  request: FastAPI request (carries auth and store).
  identity: Authenticated reader.
  part: Which file, as ``GET .../parts`` numbers it; ``-1`` holds turns
    backfilled from the retired event log.
  after_idx: Exclusive lower bound on idx (cursor-based paging).
  limit: Max rows per page.
  plaintext_only: Omit ciphertext.
  asker: The account the configured assistant reads for.
  chat: The conversation the configured assistant reads into.

Returns:
  result: ReadRecordsResponse with matching records.

post.description:
Append one file's records, resolving its part server-side.

The manifest is upserted BEFORE the records, deliberately: it is what
assigns the part number the records are keyed by, and it bounds every
reader (``idx < records``). Writing records first would briefly expose
rows no manifest accounts for.

A body naming no file carries only slash commands -- a command is typed
into the SESSION, and one submitted before the CLI has written a
transcript has no part to belong to.

A science chat holds one part per run that answered in it, and the key whose
first write opened a part alone writes it after: another key's write is 403,
so one run never rewrites another's lines.

Args:
  session_id: AgentSession ID to append to.
  request: FastAPI request (carries auth and store).
  body: Records, manifest, and slash commands to append.
  identity: Authenticated writer or viewer who opened this session.

Returns:
  result: AppendRecordsResponse with row counts.

Take what a run says it is doing, for Chat to show.

The run reports between its drains, so a change shows at once, not after the
drain it is parked in. The state stays on the session's lease: it lapses with it,
and a drain of the same run leaves it as it is, so a run says a state other than
idle again while it holds; only a change rechecks open canvases. It is the run's own
word about its
own run, shown and never trusted. A report from a run other than the one holding
the lease, or while none does, changes nothing, and is answered the same.

``taken_over`` is the report that matters: Chat then refuses the chat's lines with
409 ``chat_taken_over``, until a reattach starts a headless run again.

The caller is held to the rules of the session's drain: its opening key, or for a
chat answered by a CLI its starter's run (403 otherwise), and never the
assistant's (409 ``provider_is_cli``).

Args:
  session_id: The session the run drains.
  body: The state, and the run's own id.
  request: Starlette request object.
  identity: Authenticated run.

get.description:
Read recent conversation turns without transferring intervening tools.

Args:
  session_id: AgentSession ID to read from.
  request: FastAPI request carrying auth and store.
  identity: Authenticated reader.
  limit: Maximum user and assistant turns, from 1 through 100.
  asker: The account the configured assistant reads for.
  chat: The conversation the configured assistant reads into.

Returns:
  result: The newest turns in display order across session parts.

put.description:
Move a session to one of the caller's workspaces.

The canvas made for the session moves with it when no other session sits on it.

Args:
  session_id: The session, which the caller owns.
  body: The destination workspace Issue.
  request: Request carrying the database engine and store.
  identity: The session's account, as a browser or as its own key.

post.description:
Open a terminal on one of the caller's machines.

A browser session opens the owner's terminal. The configured assistant may open
only a detached campaign run for an attested writer or admin named as ``asker``;
every other key, service account or foreign origin is refused. The machine must
be online and its host must have asked for terminals within 45 seconds
(the machine host does by default). Attach with the ticket within 30 seconds.

Args:
  body: The machine, the terminal's size, and the canvas it opens from.
  request: Request carrying the store and the terminal hub.
  identity: The signed-in owner.
  asker: The person the configured assistant starts a campaign for.

Returns:
  opened: The terminal id and the one-use attach ticket.

Raises:
  HTTPException: 403 for an untrusted key, a service account or a foreign origin;
    404 for no such machine of the asker, or canvas; 409 ``terminal_unconfirmed`` until the
    owner confirms a machine a key enrolled, ``cli_not_installed`` when the machine's
    facts do not list the CLI asked for, ``terminal_not_enabled`` when the host is
    not asking, ``chat_run_live`` when a run is already attached to the ``attach``
    session, whether opened here or started by hand; 429 ``terminal_limit`` past 10
    opens a minute. Every terminal route answers 403 on a server with authentication
    off.

get.description:
List the caller's own machines, and their live terminals for a canvas.

The configured assistant names the person it answers as ``owner`` and lists that
person's machines, so it offers a terminal only on one they have. It opens none:
only the person's own browser does.

Args:
  request: Request carrying the store and the terminal hub.
  identity: The signed-in owner, or the assistant's agent key.
  canvas: The canvas whose live terminals to list.
  owner: The person the assistant lists for, a writer or admin; only the
    assistant may name one.

Returns:
  machines: The owner's machines, newest first, each with whether it can take a
    terminal now; and ``terminals``, the owner's live terminals opened from
    ``canvas``.

Raises:
  HTTPException: 403 ``terminal_forbidden`` for a key, a service account, anyone
    but the assistant naming an ``owner``, and an owner who is not a writer.

post.description:
Confirm a machine the caller owns, so terminals may open on it.

A machine enrolled with an API key is unconfirmed: an agent could have enrolled a
host the person does not control. Only the person, in a browser session, confirms.

Args:
  name: The machine's name.
  request: Request carrying the database engine.
  identity: The signed-in owner.

Raises:
  NotFoundError: The caller owns no such machine.

Mint a one-use ticket to attach again to the caller's live terminal.

Args:
  terminal_id: The terminal.
  request: Request carrying the terminal hub.
  identity: The signed-in opener.

Returns:
  ticket: Valid for 30 seconds, once.

Stop the caller's terminal; its shell is killed.

Args:
  terminal_id: The terminal.
  request: Request carrying the terminal hub.
  identity: The signed-in opener.

get.description:
List the org layer's variables by name; a secret's value is ``null``.

Args:
  request: Request carrying the database engine.
  identity: Writer-role principal.

Returns:
  variables: Every org-layer variable, sorted by name.

delete.description:
Delete one org-layer variable and, for a secret, its stored value.

Args:
  name: The environment-variable name.
  request: Request carrying the database engine and secret backend.
  identity: Admin principal.

Returns:
  empty: 204 with no body.

Raises:
  ValidationError: The URL's last segment is not the name.
  NotFoundError: No such variable.
  HTTPException: 503 when it is a secret and no secret store is configured.

put.description:
Set one org-layer variable.

A name stored as a secret stays secret: a plain value is refused until the
variable is deleted. A plain name may become a secret.

Args:
  name: The environment-variable name.
  body: The value and whether it is secret.
  request: Request carrying the database engine and secret backend.
  identity: Admin principal, recorded as who set it.

Returns:
  empty: 204 with no body, so a secret is never echoed.

Raises:
  ValidationError: The URL's last segment is not the name, or the value is
    too long in UTF-8 or holds a NUL.
  ConflictError: A plain value for a name stored as a secret.
  HTTPException: 503 when a secret is sent and no secret store is configured.

get.description:
Return the running server's build SHA.

``{"sha": "<hex>"}`` when known (from ``$TRACKINIZER_SHA`` or the
checkout's ``git HEAD``), else ``{"sha": "unknown"}``. A 404 instead
means the live binary predates this endpoint -- itself a staleness
signal.

Returns:
  version: Dict with 'sha' key containing build commit hash or 'unknown'.

schema.title: Response Version Route Api Version Get

get.description: List visual definitions and the default without loading visual data.

Read typed research links without requiring a launch or a single parent.

Args:
  record_id: The selected inquiry UUID.
  request: Request carrying the Store.
  direction: Read incoming or outgoing stored edges.
  edge_kind: Relationship kinds, defaulting to taxonomy and provenance.
  peer_kind: Restrict peers to one inquiry kind.
  page_size: Distinct peer quota, at most fifty.
  cursor: Continuation bound to this record and these filters.

Returns:
  page: Selected record, peer records, directed edges and continuation.

Return the lineage and timeline of a record of any kind, with hard bounded SQL.

The anchor Issue supplies `leads` (its `narrows` ancestors, at most three,
farthest first), results, and directions. An Issue is its own anchor; an
Experiment is anchored on its sole Issue producer; any other kind stays
the record and takes its sole `produced_by` Issue as its nearest lead.
Multiple producers or broader Issues stop the overview's ancestry spine;
all origins remain available through the paged lineage endpoint.

Args:
  record_id: Selected record UUID, of any kind.
  request: Request with the shared Store.
  direction_limit: Direct child Issues to return; the catalog sets the default
    and maximum.
  results_per_direction: Experiments per Issue; the catalog sets the default
    and maximum.

Returns:
  timeline: Bounded record, result, and signed evidence projection.

Cross-session captured-turn feed for the multi-agent console.

Interleaves every session's turns into one time-ordered stream so the
console shows many agents at once.

``after_created`` / ``after_session`` / ``after_part`` / ``after_seq``
together form the composite keyset cursor a poll resumes past (all are
required; the order key is composite so a bare ``created`` resume would
skip same-instant ties, and ``part`` joined it when the feed moved to IR
records -- position restarts within each source file). ``since`` / ``until``
bound a fixed historical window; ``actor`` / ``room`` / ``cli`` / ``kind`` /
``whose`` filter and ``hidden`` keeps ``private`` sessions (:func:`feed_scope`),
and ``conversation=true`` keeps only what the facets count as conversation.
``tail=true`` returns the
newest page (the live console's first load) so a backlog does not force a
replay from the beginning. The response carries ``next_after`` (a composite
cursor) for the next poll; an empty page echoes the supplied cursor so the
tail does not rewind.

``before_created`` / ``before_session`` / ``before_part`` / ``before_seq``
form an exclusive upper cursor in the same order. With ``tail=true`` they
read the preceding page without repeating a same-instant boundary.

Args:
  request: FastAPI request object for middleware access.
  identity: Authenticated user, validated to have viewer role.
  scope: Which sessions and record kinds to read.
  after_created: Resume cursor: creation timestamp of last-seen turn.
  after_session: Resume cursor: session id of last-seen turn.
  after_part: Resume cursor: part index within the session.
  after_seq: Resume cursor: sequence number within the part.
  before_created: Upper cursor: creation timestamp of the oldest turn held.
  before_session: Upper cursor: session id of the oldest turn held.
  before_part: Upper cursor: part index within the session.
  before_seq: Upper cursor: sequence number within the part.
  since: Absolute window start (inclusive).
  until: Absolute window end (inclusive).
  conversation: Keep only conversation, what a person or agent said.
  limit: Maximum turns to return.
  tail: Return newest page first (true) or oldest available (false).

Returns:
  feed: Turns across the sessions the caller reads, pagination cursor for next
    poll. A session whose transcript the caller does not read has no turn here.

Count the feed between ``since`` and ``until`` by session, room and kind.

The counts are of the records ``/feed`` returns for the same window and
filters, so the console can list agents, rooms and verbosity levels with
their sizes before it loads any of them. An agent whose run is polling says
in ``state`` what the run is doing, such as ``taken_over`` after someone opened
its CLI in a terminal, which the console offers to reattach.

Args:
  request: FastAPI request object for middleware access.
  identity: Authenticated user, validated to have viewer role.
  scope: Which sessions and record kinds to count.
  since: Window start (inclusive); unset counts from the first record.
  until: Window end (inclusive); unset counts to the last.

Returns:
  facets: Per session, room and record kind, what the window holds of the
    sessions the caller reads.

Count the feed's records per time bucket, over at most the last 7 days.

Buckets have a round width (seconds up to hours, then whole days), the
finest that fits the span in at most ``buckets``, and start on a multiple of
it from the Unix epoch; every bucket from the one holding ``since`` through
the one holding ``until`` is listed, empty ones as 0. A ``since`` more than
7 days ago starts the span 7 days ago.

Args:
  request: FastAPI request object for middleware access.
  identity: Authenticated user, validated to have viewer role.
  scope: Which sessions and record kinds to count.
  since: Span start; unset starts at the first record of the last 7 days.
  until: Span end; unset ends now.
  buckets: Most buckets to return, 2 to 1000.

Returns:
  histogram: The grid and each bucket's record count, oldest first, of the
    sessions the caller reads.

Raises:
  HTTPException: 400 for ``buckets`` outside 2 to 1000, an ``until`` before
    ``since``, or an ``until`` more than 7 days ago.

Single inquiry + edges + backlinks + recent changes, for the SPA.

``self`` is the inquiry as ``GET /api/inquiries/{id}`` serves it, unset fields
``null``, less the relation fields: ``edges`` and ``backlinks`` carry those,
grouped by edge kind with each peer's title and status. ``changes`` holds the
latest 50, newest first.

Args:
  target_id: UUID of the node to fetch.
  request: FastAPI request object for middleware access.
  identity: Authenticated user, validated to have viewer role.

Returns:
  view: ``self``, ``edges``, ``backlinks`` and ``changes``.

Return the inquiry graph as typed nodes + directed edges, for the SPA.

At most ``limit`` nodes, at least 1, and the edges between them. The newest
inquiries come first, each followed by the older ones it links to in either
direction, so an old-but-still-cited node (e.g. a foundational paper a new
belief proves) stays in view; selection stops at ``limit``. Every edge joins
two returned nodes.

With ``focus``, the nodes are instead the focus and the inquiries nearest it
(:func:`read_neighbourhood`): all within one edge, in either direction, before
any two away, and so on to ``hops``, newest first within a hop, until
``limit``. Each node then carries ``hops``, its distance from the focus.

Nodes are the light projection (id, kind, seq, title, status, created,
belief judgement/confidence), ordered by ``created`` ascending so the replay
animation adds them in authoring order; edges carry ``from_id`` -> ``to_id``,
``edge_kind``, and ``valence`` when present. The detail view
(:func:`web_get`) serves the full per-kind fields for one node on demand.

Args:
  request: FastAPI request object for middleware access.
  identity: Authenticated user, validated to have viewer role.
  limit: Most nodes to return, neighbours included, at least 1; 1000, or 60
    with a ``focus``, when unset.
  focus: The inquiry whose neighbourhood to return; unset returns the newest.
  hops: With ``focus``, the most edges to walk from it, 1 to 3.

Returns:
  graph: Nodes and edges for replay visualization, ordered by created time.

Raises:
  HTTPException: 400 for a ``limit`` below 1 or ``hops`` outside 1 to 3; 404
    when ``focus`` names no inquiry.

get.description:
Hybrid session search: embeddings + scoped tsvector, RRF-merged.

Runs the full-text arm always, and the semantic arm only when ``semantic``
is requested AND a session embedder is available. With no embedder the route
degrades to full-text-only rather than 500 -- a keyword search must never
trigger a model load -- and flags the degrade in the response
(``degraded: true``, ``semantic: false``). The query embedding uses the
embedder's query-side prefix; the corpus stayed prefix-free at ingest.

  q: The search query. Full-text terms feed ``websearch_to_tsquery``.
  identity: Authenticated user, validated to have viewer role.

    session embedder is available.
  limit: Maximum merged hits, 1-200.

    embedder to query INSTEAD of the serving default (its rows must already
    be swept). Unknown names are a 400. Empty uses the process default.

    accepts any dim in its range); must agree with any ``@dim`` in ``model``.

    configured assistant every one it reads, since it holds none of the

Stream probe frames on the caller's schedule, to test the proxy path.

Answers what the live stream meets between this server and a browser
without a redeploy: whether a hop holds the headers until the first body
byte (a late ``first_after_sec``), whether it cuts an idle stream
(``every_sec`` 0 and a long ``for_sec``), and whether ``forbid_transform``
changes either. Each frame is ``data: {"seq": n, "t": <seconds since the
request>}``, so a client can tell a frame held on the way from one sent
late. The server ends the stream at ``for_sec``, so an earlier end is a
proxy's cut.

Args:
  identity: Authenticated user, validated to have viewer role.
  first_after_sec: Seconds before the first frame; none at or past
    ``for_sec``.
  every_sec: Seconds between frames after the first, at least 0.01; 0
    sends one frame.
  for_sec: Seconds until the server ends the stream.
  forbid_transform: Send ``Cache-Control: no-transform``, which tells a proxy
    not to compress or otherwise rewrite the body.

Returns:
  stream: Server-sent probe frames.

Raises:
  HTTPException: 400 when a duration is outside ``[0, 600]``, ``for_sec``
    is 0, or ``every_sec`` is between 0 and 0.01.

post.description:
Clear the session cookie and redirect the user back to ``/``.

Logout mutates the session cookie, so it is a state-changing POST that a
cross-origin page could trigger under ``SameSite=Lax`` (which allows
top-level same-site requests to carry the cookie) -- a forced-logout CSRF.
Reject a request whose ``Origin`` (or, as a fallback, ``Referer``) names a
different origin than this server's; a request with neither header (a
non-browser client such as the CLI) has no CSRF vector and is allowed.

Args:
  request: HTTP request with Origin/Referer for CSRF validation.

Returns:
  response: 302 redirect to '/' with session cookie cleared.
